newsitem.title: UK: Marks and Spencer profits up 11 pct.
newsitem.headline: Marks and Spencer profits up 11 pct.

text.p: Britain's biggest clothing retailer Marks & Spencer Plc on Tuesday reported an 11 percent increase in first half profits and said it would add 2,000 new jobs in Britain this year.

Pretax profits in the half year to September 28 rose to 430.1 million pounds ($704.2 million) from 385.4 million. Sales increased nine percent to 3.53 billion pounds. The group raised its dividend by 10 percent to 3.3 pence. The group, which also has stores in North America, continental Europe and Asia, said it would take on the additional UK staff during its 1996/97 financial year. This would increase costs, but was essential for customer service.
Chairman Sir Richard Greenbury said consumer confidence seemed to be returning in Britain, where sales were up by 8.4 percent to 221 million pounds.
"We have increased our market share in clothing, and have held our position in foods. We have maintained our margins across the business," he said in a statement.

Overseas sales, including franchises, rose 12 percent to 591 million pounds. Initial sales at the group's first store in Germany, which opened in Cologne at the beginning of October, were well above estimate, Greenbury said. ($1=.6107 Pound)
